proposal.summary: All three current winners -- data-mlflow (v3.16.1), inspect-ai (0.3.266), foundation-agent-retrieval-bench (v0.2.1) -- earn their status on freshly re-verified evidence, and this layer's recorded open_gaps/catalog text (conv/layers.json; catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json; catalogs/us-equities/{data-research,foundation-memory,agents-operations}.json) is stale: a pre-registered, hash-verified execution wave dated 2026-09-23 (evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/) already ran nearly every check the open_gaps still list as missing, three days before this review -- its own limits sections say updating the catalog text "is left to the coordinator." Most decisive: the exact promptfoo-vs-inspect-ai matched trial the open_gaps called for was run TWICE (an 8-case deterministic mock arm and a separate 30-case real-embedding-scorer arm) and settled both times with 100% cross-harness scoring agreement; inspect-ai edged ahead on frozen-source byte-fidelity (8/8 vs 6/8), self-contained retry-error provenance, and wall-clock. The project's own recorded verdict: "supports keeping inspect-ai selected... not a model-quality win." So promptfoo is not a verified challenger here -- merit, actually checked, favors the incumbent. mlflow was independently re-confirmed current (its README directly refutes comet-ml/opik's demonstrated_gap, matching the project's own 2026-09-23 adversarial verification) and shown bound to a real hash-verified replay of this project's own chronological research evaluation. foundation-agent-retrieval-bench's one recorded weakness (Darwin-arm64-only execution) was independently retired by a byte-identical Linux x86_64 rerun. Checked and correctly non-winning: opik (refuted), phoenix (Elastic-2.0 self-host restriction, narrower scope, already catalogued -- not a blind spot), river (real causality-probe-verified execution, but an honest negative predictive result), and three newly-surfaced small repos (TraderHarness/Lacuna/falsification-ledger) independently confirmed to exist but off-requirement for this layer (they validate trading-strategy backtests, not agent/experiment infrastructure -- fit backtesting-engine/strategy-research instead). Four 2026 papers confirmed real via direct abstract fetch are useful methodology inputs, not installable candidates. No verified challenger survives against any winner. Recommend only two low-cost housekeeping actions: bump the inspect-ai pin past 0.3.266 (already run successfully at 0.3.268 within this same wave; PyPI is now at 0.3.269) and have the coordinator refresh the stale catalog/open_gaps text to cite the 2026-09-23 receipts instead of describing these three winners as unexecuted.

winner_status.note: Pin v3.16.1 = exact current upstream (gh api releases/latest + PyPI json, both checked 2026-09-26). Its README directly confirms 'Built on OpenTelemetry... supporting any LLM provider and agent framework' plus 'Choose from 50+ built-in metrics and LLM judges' -- independently corroborating the project's own 2026-09-23 adversarial verification that refuted comet-ml/opik's demonstrated_gap (disposition refuted_targeted_candidate, survives:false). The catalog's own text calling mlflow's workflow 'Prospective and UNEXECUTED' (catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json) is now stale: evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/us-equities__evaluation-experiments/{1-five-package-installs,8-research-evaluation-mlflow-binding}.json show it actually installed, health-checked (loopback server, /health OK), and bound to a hash-verified replay of this project's own chronological research evaluation -- 16 params, 19 metrics and 9 dataset digests logged and read back with 0 mismatches, both injected negative probes (ledger_records+1, exit-code 999) correctly caught, replay equal to the 2026-09-19 receipt (same ledger sha256, 21/21 selection hashes). No verified better alternative survives.

Pin 0.3.266 is 3 PyPI patches behind current 0.3.269 (confirmed directly; GitHub itself publishes no Releases object for this repo, 404 confirmed) -- a real but modest recording lag, not neglect: this same wave already ran 0.3.268 successfully (evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/foundation__quality-evaluation/9-inspect-mlflow-local-vllm.json -- real local-vLLM inference, hello_world exact 1.000, security_guide model_graded_fact 0.688, logged cleanly to mlflow). The exact matched promptfoo-vs-inspect-ai trial this layer's own open_gaps called for is done, twice, both 'settled' 2026-09-23: an 8-case deterministic mock comparison (.../us-equities__evaluation-experiments/{0,2}-*.json) and a 30-case real-embedding-scorer comparison (.../foundation__quality-evaluation/4-promptfoo-vs-inspect-ai.json). Both show 100% cross-harness scoring agreement (identical predictions on every case); inspect-ai leads on byte-exact frozen-source retention (8/8 vs 6/8 gate-source hashes), self-contained retry-error provenance (kept in the final eval log vs promptfoo's side-channel-only log plus an overwritten primary output), and wall-clock (4.2s vs 12.7s, one observation). The project's own recorded verdict: 'supports keeping inspect-ai selected for the harness properties measured here... not a model-quality win.' Recommend a pin bump to 0.3.268/0.3.269 as housekeeping, not a challenge.

Confirmed independently via gh api 8 stars, MIT, v0.2.1 tag exact match, pushed 2026-08-04 -- 53 days quiet as of 2026-09-26, a real slowdown (single maintainer, 1 open issue) but far under the 12-month unmaintained bar. Already the only layer winner with actual executed evidence at the 2026-09-22 claude/codex lane adjudication (2/2 evidence-reviewer votes cited real pytest '15 passed' plus real retrieval-metric runs). Its sole recorded weakness at that adjudication -- 'recorded on Darwin arm64, not this PC' -- was independently retired on 2026-09-23: an unmodified rerun on Linux x86_64 reproduced the Darwin receipt's per-sample detail files byte-identical (sha256-matched) for both lexical and BM25 rankers across all 101 samples, 15/15 upstream tests passing (evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/us-equities__evaluation-experiments/4-arb-trace2code-host-rerun.json). Residual, real, and correctly un-closed-by-rerun: its proven scope is file-level code retrieval (gin/click = 82/101 samples), not financial-document retrieval -- no better-evidenced alternative fills that specific gap either (mteb overlaps only in evaluating embeddings/STS, a different task, and its own pin is behind upstream).

rejected.name: online-ml/river
rejected.reason: Executed for real, 2026-09-23, settled: a causality-probe-verified delayed-progressive-validation check on real bundled LEAN SPY daily data (0 causality violations in the delayed run vs 1,797 in the immediate positive control, proving the delay mechanism actually works). But the logistic model showed no predictive edge -- delayed 0.592 / immediate 0.610 accuracy, both beaten by a naive prior-class baseline at 0.612 -- an honest negative result. Remains conditional: applies only if streaming/online updates are independently justified; doesn't address this layer's telemetry/broker-isolation requirement.

claude_verify_checks.name: candidate:temporal-leakage:core-claims
claude_verify_checks.claim: proves recency effect is mathematically indistinguishable from leakage in a passive backtest alone; proposes reference-point methods (known cutoff or matched control) for an adjusted score; validates via twin-model leakage injection; on frontier models finds 1 real cutoff-leakage signature and clears 5 models whose apparent edge was recency bias
claude_verify_checks.note: Fetched abstract confirms near-verbatim: 'we prove no passive backtest can separate the two from genuine skill... A known cutoff identifies leakage at the boundary; a matched clean control identifies it globally and yields a leakage-adjusted score... Deployed on frontier models, they detect one cutoff-localized signature and... clear five models whose apparent advantages were recency alone.' Every element of the candidate's claim is directly supported.
